summary: PR 5201 auth-browser gate PASSED in full at the exact head 0355023c3170c87a84cd9e5688ae6b4f3e4df3ae (fork head re-verified live at filing; clean normal clone; Chrome for Testing 157.0.8103.50 with its matching driver). SELENIUM LEGS: focused explorer test passed 1/1 at seed A6429A38B2BCEB3A; the combined suite passed at seed E26F868A06F9131C (AdminUiSecurityAuthTest 2/2, AdminUiSmokeTest 5/5), from fresh JUnit XML. TIDY: zero changes. ROOT CHECK -x test in the normal clone PASSED. One environment incident is disclosed, not hidden: the first installDist and check attempts failed on file writes because the per-user disk quota was exhausted by accumulated gate clones (the cached jars and sources verified intact); after deleting five disposable clones of already-filed gates, both legs were rerun from the same head and passed cleanly (installDist exit 0, check exit 0 with zero failed tasks). PACKAGED LEGS (installDist server, BasicAuthPlugin configuration identical to the test harness, production headers): unauthenticated requests returned 401 on both the admin and /api paths, authenticated 200; the served /solr/index.html carries the production CSP (frame-ancestors 'none', frame-src 'self') and X-Frame-Options DENY; the V2 API answers at the server root (/api/collections 200, /solr/api/collections 404, which is how the explorer's relative server URL resolves in the packaged layout). Driven in a real browser against the packaged server: login, explorer collections request returned 200 with a collections array, the Authorization header equal to the session's stored header, and X-Requested-With set. CREDENTIAL REVOCATION (the assignment's runtime question, previously only source-traced): after the password was rotated through the authentication API, the explorer's next request replayed the stored, now-dead header and received 401, with the stale header still present in sessionStorage afterwards; the Admin UI's next request then cleared the stored header and presented the login screen; after logging in with the new password, the explorer's next request returned 200 with the new header. So the divergence the adjacent investigation traced is real at runtime and recovery is exactly: re-authenticate in the Admin UI. A no-role user's explorer request returned 403, rendered in the explorer without a redirect. CROSS-ORIGIN BOUNDARY: a page served from a different origin could frame the explorer page (it carries no framing headers of its own, by design of the embed), but could not read the explorer's sessionStorage (blocked by the same-origin policy) and its own cross-origin fetch to /api/collections was blocked with no Authorization sent; the foreign origin's storage held no header. FAIL-BEFORE: the unchanged revised test on contributor parent 3f9faa9e9861ce28f3ede3f4305bd91b6e297463 (overlay file SHA-256 identical to the round-2 record) reaches the request and fails at the collections-response wait, executed in the sibling selector investigation at identical head, parent, and seed and re-evidenced in this gate's archive. JWT was not exercised (the harness and this packaged setup configure BasicAuth only); the adjacent investigation's findings (the disableJsClient Scalar npm dependency, generated-client metadata, proxy and bundle questions) stand as separately reported and are not restated as gate proof. No source was changed; the PR is untouched.
